messages:
Alice (Support): Peregrine Health (dedicated tenant peregrine-42) reporting sudden 429 surge starting ~00:00 UTC. Multiple routes affected, dashboards flapping. Root TS 1777777771.

Alice (Support): customer report: 'hundreds of 429s/min for ~10m, dashboard write failures, webhooks retrying'. They don't see increased downstream traffic.

Jordan (CE): need sample request-id + response headers so we can confirm x-rate-limit headers and Retry-After.

Alice (Support): pasted sample from their edge: 
```
REQUEST_ID=9f3e1b2c
route=/v1/chat/completions
status=429
headers={
  \"x-rate-limit-rpm\": \"1200\",
  \"x-rate-limit-tpm\": \"20000\",
  \"x-rate-limit-reset\": \"25\",
  \"retry-after\": \"10\"
}
```
They included ~15 request_ids within a 2-minute window hitting 429.

Mateo (SRE): header shape implies RPM bucket overflow. Two leading suspects: concurrent token refresh stampede or cron/cron-like jobs aligning on minute boundaries. Do they run hourly top-of-hour refreshes?

Alice (Support): Customer confirms: they deployed a new rollout and enabled a top-of-hour token refresh across ~150 worker processes to avoid stale tokens. That lines up with the spike.

Jordan (CE): classic refresh stampede. Short mitigation suggestions to send to customer:
- immediately stop or stagger the scheduled refresh (add jitter)
- honor Retry-After + exponential backoff in SDK clients
- enable short-term quota bump / burst window on our side until they roll changes

Mateo (SRE): infra-side actions I'll take: enable per-tenant smoothing, allow a small burst allowance for peregrine-42 for 60m, and add a temporary fallback route to a lower-cost model for non-critical endpoints. Also create alert rule for 429 rate >5% sustained 3m.

Priya (Acct Mgmt): customer impact is visible. Offer temp quota bump & a plain-language runbook for their ops team. They want steps they can follow quickly.

Jordan (CE): Draft runbook (short):
1) Immediately pause the scheduled refresh job or flip it to manual run.
2) Short-term: update SDKs to read Retry-After and perform jittered backoff. Example (node):
```
async function attempt(req){
  for(let i=0;i<5;i++){
    const res = await fetch(req);
    if(res.status !== 429) return res;
    const ra = parseInt(res.headers.get('retry-after')) || (2**i);
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ra*1000 + Math.floor(Math.random()*1500)));
  }
  throw new Error('retries exhausted');
}
```
3) Long-term: randomize token refresh across workers (jitter window 5-10min) and implement client-side leaky-bucket to smooth bursts.

Alice (Support): sent runbook + temp quota bump offer. Customer accepted 1-hour bump and agreed to roll immediate staggered change.

Mateo (SRE): internal explanation for the thread: Dedicated enforces both RPM and TPM. Minute-level refill can be overwhelmed by many concurrent callers within the same minute even if overall throughput (TPM) is within limits. The ingress minute bucket overflows and we return 429 with Retry-After indicating seconds until reset.

Mateo (SRE): infra changes applied:
- tenant smoothing enabled for peregrine-42
- 30s burst allowance for 60 minutes
- fallback routing to model-compact for non-critical routes
- alert SD-7892 created if 429-rate > 5% for 3m

support-bot: Ticket created SD-7892 \"Peregrine: refresh stampede — temp smoothing & bump\" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SD-7892

Alice (Support): customer rolled out staggered refresh and disabled cron. Monitoring shows 429s dropped to near zero within ~90s of change. They confirmed dashboards recovered.

Jordan (CE): internal repro steps (do not send to customer):
- spawn N=150 concurrent clients that perform token refresh then 3 immediate API calls to the same tenant
- observe x-rate-limit headers and 429s when minute bucket overflows
Quick repro command:
```
for i in {1..150}; do
  (curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/auth/refresh && curl -s -X POST https://staging.redwood/v1/generate) &
done; wait
```

Mateo (SRE): follow-ups: keep smoothing in place for 1 hour and monitor. If customer deploys jitter, remove burst allowance. Filing docs ticket to add onboarding guidance about token refresh staggering and sample SDK reading of x-rate-limit headers.

Priya (Acct Mgmt): customer appreciates rapid response. We'll schedule a short follow-up meeting to ensure jitter rollout goes smoothly during a maintenance window.

Alice (Support): notes to include in final customer-facing message:
- root cause: simultaneous token refresh + fanout saturated per-minute RPM bucket
- immediate mitigations we applied: temporary quota bump, tenant smoothing, fallback routing
- recommended permanent fixes: stagger refreshes, honor Retry-After with jitter/backoff, implement client-side smoothing
- attaching SDK snippet + cron-jitter example

Mateo (SRE): keeping ownership for monitoring until 02:30 UTC. Marking incident as mitigated; will close after 1h of healthy metrics.

Alice (Support): closing thread for now — will append final summary when smoothing removed.
